title: Audits, Assessments and Security Awareness

header.html: 5.5 Explain concepts associated with audit and assessment activities; 5.6 Given a scenario, apply security awareness concepts to improve organizational security
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Audits and assessments

Term Meaning
Audit A formal, independent examination against a standard or policy
Assessment An evaluation of controls or risk, often less formal
Gap analysis Compare current state with the target to find missing controls
Benchmarking Compare against peers or a standard

Data gathering

Sampling (check part of the population), questionnaires and surveys, interviews, assertion (a statement by management that something is true), and reference sources such as:

Reference Use
MITRE ATT&CK A catalog of attacker tactics and techniques
Cyber Kill Chain Stages of an attack (reconnaissance to actions on objectives)
Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis Relates adversary, capability, infrastructure and victim

Scoping and engagement types

Item Meaning
Audit charter The document that gives the audit authority and scope
Frequency How often audits take place
Internal Compliance checks, audit committee, self-assessments
External Examinations, assessments, regulatory audits, independent third-party audits

Exam tip

. External independent audits give the most objective assurance. Self-assessments are the least independent. A gap analysis compares today versus the standard.

2Penetration testing

A penetration test is an authorized, simulated attack to find weaknesses. Always agree rules of engagement and get written permission first.

Type Meaning
Known environment (white box) Tester has full information
Unknown environment (black box) Tester has no information
Partially known environment (gray box) Some information
Physical Tests buildings and locks
Offensive The red team attacks
Defensive The blue team defends and detects
Integrated Red and blue work together (purple)
Reconnaissance Passive (public information, no contact with the target) or active (probing the target)

Other topics: frameworks and standards (industry, international and region-specific), functional testing (does it do what it should), behavioral testing (how it behaves under unusual input).

Exam tip

. Passive recon = no contact (search engines, public records). Active recon = touches the target (port scan). Unknown environment = black box. Never test without written authorization.

3Security awareness

Topic Details
Types of training Initial or onboarding, ongoing, targeted (by role or risk), corrective (after a failure, for example a phishing click)
Delivery mechanisms Learning management system (LMS), self-service portals, one-to-one, one-to-many
Reporting and monitoring effectiveness Metrics, managerial reports, personnel behavior risk scoring
Common topics Social engineering, emerging security topics, password and credential management, remote work and hybrid work, BYOD, business email compromise (BEC), removable media and cables, situational awareness, operational security

Measuring success: phishing simulation click rates, reporting rates, training completion, and incident trends. Reward reporting, do not punish it.

Exam tip

. BEC is an email fraud where an attacker impersonates an executive or vendor to move money. Corrective training follows a failure. Targeted training matches high-risk roles (finance, executives).

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors hires a firm to test its network. The testers are given no information about the environment. Which type is this?

  • AKnown environment
  • BPartially known environment
  • CIntegrated
  • DUnknown environment
Show the answer

Answer: D. Testers with no prior information perform an unknown environment (black box) test.

S2A tester searches public records and social media about the company before any contact with its systems. Which activity is this?

  • AActive reconnaissance
  • BPassive reconnaissance
  • CPrivilege escalation
  • DFunctional testing
Show the answer

Answer: B. Collecting information without touching the target is passive reconnaissance.

S3An employee clicks a link in a simulated phishing email. What should the company do?

  • AFire the employee immediately
  • BProvide corrective training
  • CIgnore the result
  • DDisable email
Show the answer

Answer: B. Corrective training addresses a failure, and the goal is learning rather than punishment.

S4Which audit gives the most objective view for a regulator?

  • AAn independent third-party audit
  • BA self-assessment
  • CA manager's assertion
  • DAn informal walkthrough
Show the answer

Answer: A. Independent third-party audits are the most objective.

S5A team compares its controls with the standard it wants to meet and lists what is missing. Which activity is this?

  • ASampling
  • BGap analysis
  • CBenchmarking only
  • DTabletop exercise
Show the answer

Answer: B. A gap analysis compares the current state with the target to find gaps.

S6An attacker poses as the CEO and emails the finance team to change a vendor's bank account. Which threat does training cover here?

  • AWatering hole
  • BCache poisoning
  • CTailgating
  • DBusiness email compromise
Show the answer

Answer: D. Impersonating an executive by email to redirect payments is business email compromise.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does MITRE ATT&CK provide?

Show the answer

A catalog of attacker tactics and techniques.

R2What is the difference between passive and active reconnaissance?

Show the answer

Passive uses public information with no contact; active probes the target.

R3Which penetration test type gives the tester full information?

Show the answer

Known environment.

R4What are the four types of security awareness training?

Show the answer

Initial or onboarding, ongoing, targeted and corrective.

R5What is BEC?

Show the answer

Business email compromise: impersonating executives or vendors to move money.

R6What does an audit charter define?

Show the answer

The authority and scope of an audit.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Audits internal (compliance, audit committee, self-assessment) and external (regulatory, independent third party); gap analysis; benchmarking
Reference models MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain, Diamond Model
Pen testing known, unknown, partially known; physical, offensive, defensive, integrated; passive vs active recon; written authorization
Awareness initial, ongoing, targeted, corrective; LMS and portals; metrics and risk scoring; BEC, social engineering, BYOD, removable media
